subject: BrightLane demo: intermittent SDK reconnect -> duplicate events
messages:
From: Evan Miller <evan.miller@brightlane.health>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BrightLane demo — intermittent duplicates when reconnecting

Hi Karthik,

Quick note from this morning's demo: when our client briefly loses network and reconnects to the streaming endpoint, we sometimes see duplicate generated segments in the UI (same token sequence replayed). We collected logs and a short session trace (attached). This happened twice during a 20-minute pilot — not consistent but reproducible if we kill the connection and let the SDK auto-retry.

SDK details: node SDK 1.4.2, streaming via SSE fallback on our side. Sample client flow attached in sesh_trace.txt.

Can you loop in engineering to confirm whether the reconnect path dedups or if we need to add client-side idempotency keys? This demo is part of our purchase evaluation (deal BL-2026-332). We can pause demos if this is a blocker, but would prefer a short workaround.

Thanks,
Evan Miller
Senior Platform Engineer
BrightLane Health

Attachment: brightlane-logs.zip (logs + session traces)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-11-15T10:00:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: BrightLane demo — intermittent duplicates when reconnecting

Marissa / Dev / Laura — forwarding BrightLane's logs from a live pilot. Evan reports duplicate tokens when the client auto-reconnects to a streaming response.

Summary / ask:
- Customer: BrightLane Health (deal BL-2026-332), evaluating for a pilot ramp.
- Symptom: After a transient network drop the SDK reconnects and the UI shows duplicate generated text segments (same token seq repeated).
- Repro: Kill TCP during a long stream, let SDK reconnect. They used node SDK 1.4.2.
- Priority: high for the sale; they may pause demos without a mitigation.

Can platform/runtime confirm whether server-side dedupe exists on reconnection, or whether this is an SDK reconnection bug? If it's an SDK fix, can we scope a short patch and a recommended client workaround? Can Product advise on priority and whether this should be escalated to the release team?

Attachments: brightlane-logs.zip, sesh_trace.txt (included).

Next step: Dev — please triage and either identify root cause or ask for a repro environment. Marissa / Laura — advise prioritization/commit if we need a fast patch for the deal.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T14:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightLane demo — intermittent duplicates when reconnecting

Thanks for the context and the logs. I started a quick pass on the attached trace. A few initial questions / observations: 

1) The session trace shows the client received the final chunk, then lost the connection, and the SDK reconnected and resumed from a non-0 offset. The sequence numbers in the trace suggest the server returned overlapping token ranges on reconnect (i.e. 0..120 then 110.. onwards).

2) Can you confirm the exact SDK call pattern the customer used (send a single request + stream vs multiple streaming chunks)? The repro would be easier with their short snippet from sesh_trace.txt — looks like an auto-retry wrapper around fetch.

3) I created JIRA SUP-4521 to track the root cause (link in related links) and uploaded the logs.

Hypothesis: two plausible causes — (A) server-side resume logic doesn’t correctly honor client resume offsets when the session token is stale, or (B) the SDK's reconnect code replays buffered tokens without dedupe when the transport resets. From the trace I lean slightly toward (B), but need a minimal repro.

Immediate asks:
- Karthik: can you ask Evan for the exact SDK call (snippet) and confirm whether they enabled any explicit idempotency token or stream-resume flag?
- Marissa / Laura: if this is a customer-blocker for the deal, recommend we prioritize a short-term SDK patch to dedupe on reconnect (guard at client layer) vs a server change. SDK patch is lower blast radius and faster.

I'll allocate time tomorrow to build a reproducer against our staging runtime and will post findings. If I get a repro that proves SDK is the cause I'll open a hotfix branch.

- Dev
Principal Runtime Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightLane demo — intermittent duplicates when reconnecting

Thanks for triaging this, Dev. Quick product/PM response and recommended plan.

Short answer: we should treat this as a high-priority field bug because it impacts demo reliability and customer trust. Given the timeline on the deal, I recommend the following path: 

Options (ordered by speed/risk):
1) Short SDK patch (recommended): add a reconnect dedupe guard that checks the last-sent token offset and suppresses overlapping tokens on resume. Low blast radius, can ship a patch to node SDK 1.4.x line. Target: staging patch by 2026-11-20, prod release 2026-11-24 if QA passes.

2) Server-side resume fix: ensure resume offsets are honored and never return overlapping sequences. More invasive; schedule to next sprint (T+3 weeks).

3) Customer workaround: ask BrightLane to enable client-side idempotency/unique request IDs and/or reduce automated reconnects during streaming. This is least-desirable for user experience but we can offer as an immediate mitigation.

Action items: 
- Dev: if you can confirm SDK repro (by EOD tomorrow), open a hotfix PR and tag Release Engineering.
- Karthik: please share the exact snippet from BrightLane and ask if they can test the recommended workaround (idempotency header) while we work the patch.
- Laura: can you approve hotfix priority and commit 1 engineer-day from the release team if we move forward?

I'll update the HubSpot deal record with the mitigation plan and proposed timeline. Also added JIRA SUP-4521 to our sprint board.

Thanks all — keep me posted on repro status and I'll coordinate comms with the customer.

Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference
